text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Amer deputy manager Pekka Kainulainen hopes a buyer for the group will emerge soon, adding that further decisions about its future can be expected later this week.
- Trade unions agreed to start studying buffer funds against economic fluctuations in European economic and monetary union (EMU), based on joint statement in May.
- Next year's budget should set priority on lowering employers' income tax and employment costs, Confederation of Unions for Academic Professionals in Finland (AKAVA) says.
- Border traffic between Finland and Russia is a good example of smoothness, says EU transport commissioner Neil Kinnock, visiting check points at the border.
- Among gifts on President Martti Ahtisaari's 60th birthday were an honorary professorship, an "ex libris" label, and he had a Namibian school dedicated to him.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Funds for Amer deal are already in Finland, says Briton Lord Moyne, adding he is suprised by K-shareholders' sudden rejection of his offer and guarantee problems only technical.
- Norvestia is still interested in bying Amer, investment company's CEO Timo Loyttyniemi says.
- A new Nokia mobile phone model with internet service will be launched next autumn, spokesman at the telecommunications group says.
- Price hike of raw wood has boosted wood sales. In May forest owners sold 40 percent more wood than usual, sector representatives say.
AAMULEHTI
- Many Finnish bus companies want to start freight business by rail as soon as state-owned rail road company VR opens rail to others, sector representatives say.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Mobile phone maker Benefon still sees a future for NMT mobile phones, despite the rise of GSM.
- Shift work increases risk of heart disease, a Finnish medical study shows.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Financial Supervision will investigate if suspension -- and notification of suspension -- of Amer deal with Lord Moyne was done according to bourse regulations.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
